University of Michigan :: Organization and administration :: Finances :: Endowment :: chunk_0023
The university's [financial endowment](/wiki/Financial_endowment "Financial endowment"), known as the "University Endowment Fund", comprises over 12,400 individual funds. Each fund must be spent according to the donor's specifications. Approximately 28% of the total endowment is allocated to support academic programs, while 22% is designated for student scholarships and fellowships. Approximately 19% of the endowment was allocated to Michigan Medicine and can only be used to support research, patient care, or other purposes specified by donors.[[w 2]](#cite_note-154)

As of 2023, the university's endowment, valued at $17.9 billion, ranks as the tenth largest among all universities in the country.[[r 4]](#cite_note-155)[[136]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJordan2023-156) The university ranks 86th in endowment per student. The [law school](/wiki/Michigan_Law "Michigan Law")'s endowment, totaling over $500 million, has a significantly higher per-student value compared to that of its parent university. It ranks as the eighth wealthiest law school in the nation in 2022.

It is the 5th-most common cancer in UK women (around 7,100 were diagnosed in 2011) and the 5th-most common cause of cancer death in women (around 4,300 died in 2012).[[145]](#cite_note-145)[[32]](#cite_note-DynaMed15-32)[[35]](#cite_note-CRUKRisks-35) The incidence rate over the whole UK population is 21.6 per 100,000.

As of 2014, the UK saw approximately 7,000–7,100 yearly diagnoses with 4,200 deaths.[[29]](#cite_note-Jayson-29)[[35]](#cite_note-CRUKRisks-35) A 2022 article from *The Times* put the estimate at 7,500 new cases yearly in Britain.[[146]](#cite_note-thetimes2022-146) Early symptoms are often mistaken for common conditions such as cystitis or irritable bowel syndrome, and about 40 per cent of UK women wrongly believe that cervical screening detects ovarian cancer, an increase from 30 per cent in 2016.[[146]](#cite_note-thetimes2022-146)

Black women have twice the risk for sex cord-stromal tumors compared to non-Black women.[[33]](#cite_note-Williams12-33) The highest prevalence is in Caucasian and Hispanic women, followed by African-American and Asian women.[[139]](#cite_note-Gaona20-139) The highest mortality from ovarian cancer is in African-American women.[[139]](#cite_note-Gaona20-139) [Ashkenazi Jewish](/wiki/Ashkenazi_Jew "Ashkenazi Jew") women carry mutated *BRCA* alleles five times more often than the rest of the population, giving them a higher risk developing ovarian cancer.[[29]](#cite_note-Jayson-29)

Development of *Attack of the Clones* began in March 2000, some months after the release of *The Phantom Menace*. By June 2000, Lucas and Hales completed a draft of the script, and principal photography took place from June to September 2000. The film crew primarily shot at [Fox Studios Australia](/wiki/Fox_Studios_Australia "Fox Studios Australia") in Sydney, with additional footage filmed in [Tunisia](/wiki/Tunisia "Tunisia"), [Italy](/wiki/Italy "Italy") and [Spain](/wiki/Spain "Spain"). It was one of the first motion pictures shot completely on a [high-definition digital 24-frame system](/wiki/Digital_cinematography "Digital cinematography").

*Attack of the Clones* was released by [20th Century Fox](/wiki/20th_Century_Fox "20th Century Fox") in the United States on May 16, 2002. It received mixed reviews from critics; the film's increased focus on action was praised, while the characters and dialogue were regarded more critically. It performed well at the box office, making $653.8 million worldwide. Yet, it became the first *Star Wars* film to get outgrossed in its year of release, becoming the [fourth-highest-grossing film of 2002 worldwide](/wiki/2002_in_film#Highest-grossing_films "2002 in film"). *[Revenge of the Sith](/wiki/Revenge_of_the_Sith "Revenge of the Sith")* (2005) followed *Attack of the Clones*, concluding the [*Star Wars* prequel trilogy](/wiki/Star_Wars_prequel_trilogy "Star Wars prequel trilogy").
